newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: BEAZLEY SAYS SCRAP PEOPLE'S CONVENTION ON REPUBLIC
Federal Opposition Leader, Kim Beazley, is urging the Prime Minister to hold a plebiscite on the Republic, without the promised People's Convention.
Cabinet appears set to go ahead with a half-appointed, half-elected Convention later this year to canvass options for constitutional change.
Mr Beazley says the issue has already been thoroughly canvassed and a Convention would be an unnecessary complication. - - - -
PLANS TO EVACUATE CHARLEVILLE HOSPITAL
Queensland's counter-disaster team is monitoring the flood situation at Charleville in the State's south west.
A State of Disaster was declared in the town this morning as floodwaters continue to rise.
Emergency Services Minister, Mick Veivers, says arrangements have been made to begin evacuating the Hospital.
Mr Veivers told ABC Radio a local school has been set aside as an evacuation centre and a helicopter is being sent to the area to assist with rescues.
He says Charleville people are prepared in case there's a repeat of the devastaing 1990 floods.
FISCHER SAYS AUST HANDS TIED ON CAR TARIFFS
Deputy Prime Minister, Tim Fischer, says although Australia needs a strong car industry, it is bound by Asia-Pacific free trade commitments.
The Productivity Commission, in a draft report on the car industry, has recommended car tariffs be slashed to five-per-cent by the year 2004.
The proposal's being strongly resisted by car manufacturers and Coalition MP's in South Australia and Victoria, where most car manufacturing takes place.
Mr Fischer says Cabinet will be weighing the issue very carefully, but has issued a reminder about Australia's committment to achieve complete free trade by the year 2010.
KENNETT SEEKS TOP CREDIT RATING
Victoria's Premier Jeff Kennett, and Treasurer, Alan Stockdale, leave for their annual mission to the World's financial centres tonight.
The mission includes visits to London, Frankfurt, Zurich and New York.
The Premier has made it clear it's very important for Victoria to regain it's Tripple-A credit rating.
He's promised financial rewards for businesses and households if agencies give Victoria Triple-A status before the end of the century.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
